results.summary_before: The design allows experimentation with VGA timing parameters through a set of registers written over an SPI interface. It is a reconfigurable tool for exploring video modes rather than a fixed-function display controller. The design outputs a VGA video signal and uses a clock generator for timing. It is verified with a cocotb testbench.
results.summary: ROTFPGA v2 is a reconfigurable logic circuit built from identical tiles, each containing a NAND gate, a D flip-flop and a buffer, that can be individually rotated or mirrored according to configuration. It is a port of the original ROTFPGA from Caravel to TinyTapeout, reduced from 24x24 to 8x8 tiles with 8 inputs and 8 outputs. Configuration and reset use a routing-efficient scan chain, and tiles are written as hand-optimized gate-level Verilog with configuration stored in latches. The test suite sets up two configurations and runs upload, download, single-step, propagation and loop-breaker tests.

results.summary: TinyMOA-IHP0P4-8x8 is an 8x8 digital compute-in-memory core implemented in Verilog on an experimental IHP SG13G2 CMOS5L shuttle. It exposes 8 data input bits, write-enable, execute, read-next and accumulator-clear controls, along with column-select and done outputs. Results are read out on 8 output pins, with the top two marked as zero. Documentation and testing details are still in progress.

results.summary: This project is a 2x2 signed 4-bit systolic array matrix multiplier with 9-bit accumulators, overflow detection, sign reconstruction and a manual step mode. Data is loaded as an 8-bit byte with write-enable and start controls, and results are read out on 8 output bits. Status signals include busy, output-valid, 8-bit overflow, accumulator sign, manual clock and step mode. It is implemented in Verilog for Tiny Tapeout, though documentation is very thin.

results.summary_before: This design receives serial data via UART, stores it in an 8-bit register, and compares it with a pseudo-random pattern generated by an LFSR. It uses an LFSR for pattern generation and a comparator for detection. The design is notable for its use of LFSR and UART interface.
results.summary: This is the VAK FSM replacement for the VAK lab PCB board at Northwestern. It interfaces to an ADC through 12 data bits, end-of-conversion and conversion-start signals, and to SPI devices via spi_clk, MOSI and MISO. Chip selects for FRAM and LoRA, plus sensor and radio VCC enables, are provided on the outputs. It is written in SystemVerilog and will be tested locally, with no external hardware required at this time.

results.summary_before: This project is a numerically controlled oscillator (NCO) with a DAC output, capable of generating frequencies up to about 12.3 MHz. It is controlled via a parallel interface and includes a filter-analog block. The design is a compact signal-generation experiment with detailed pin-level control but no silicon test results. It is intended for audio or waveform generation applications.
results.summary: This project adds one AND gate and one NOT gate for testing. The AND gate takes IN0 and IN1 as inputs and drives OUT1, while the NOT gate takes IN2 and drives OUT2. Testing consists of checking the AND and NOT gate truth tables. OUT1 and OUT2 drive LEDs as external hardware.
